Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the daily notice generation and delivery run for all in-force life and annuity blocks; escalates missed statutory windows to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 19 (Conduct of Business) Standards 19.5-19.9 on pre-contractual and ongoing disclosure, read against the local transposition in each writing jurisdiction (US: state grace/lapse and replacement notice statutes, NAIC Model 580/613; EU: IDD Art. 20 and Solvency II policyholder information rules; UK: FCA ICOBS 6). ICP 22 Standard 22.3 risk-based-approach text re-read where a notice carries a customer due-diligence trigger

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven notice generation across policy administration: premium due and grace-period notices, lapse and reinstatement notices, replacement notices, annual statements of account, non-forfeiture option notices, adverse underwriting decision notices, annual privacy notices and beneficiary change confirmations

In-scope systems.value: Policy admin raises the trigger event; the composition engine renders the notice; images and proof-of-delivery land in OpenText Document Mgmt and are indexed on the Notice Log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Notice Generation and Delivery Procedure NGD-01 — jurisdictional notice catalogue, trigger-to-notice map, day-count rules (calendar vs business days, mailing-date rule), delivery channel hierarchy, undeliverable handling and re-issue rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved annually each January and within 30 days of any bulletin changing a notice day count or mandated wording

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per notice per policy — the day count runs from the trigger date (premium due date, lapse date, application decision date, replacement solicitation date), the tightest US windows being 5 business days for replacement notices and 30 days for grace-period and adverse-decision notices; a monthly timeliness return goes to Market Conduct by the 10th

Deadline reminders configured.value: Notice aging queue in policy admin flags each open trigger at 50% and 80% of its statutory window and breaches at 100%; breach rows page the Policy Admin Ops Lead the same business day

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Rendered notice image, template version id, address used, dispatch/postmark date, e-delivery consent record and delivery receipt retained in OpenText Document Mgmt for the life of the policy plus 7 years after termination

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every notice sent outside its statutory window, sent on a superseded template version, or never sent is raised as a conduct exception with policy number, days late, customer-detriment assessment and re-issue/rights-extension disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late-notice remediation, including the decision to extend the grace period or reinstate the policy without evidence of insurability

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All notice-triggering events raised in policy administration in the quarter — premium due dates, lapses, reinstatements, replacement solicitations, underwriting declines and policy anniversaries — by writing company and jurisdiction

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Timeliness must be 100% for replacement and grace/lapse notices (any breach is a fail); 99.5% for all other notice types; any notice rendered on a superseded template version is an automatic fail regardless of timing

checklist.step: Refresh the jurisdictional notice catalogue
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System, filter Obligations by regCode REG-013 and Category = Consumer Protection, and export the notice-bearing obligations for every jurisdiction the group writes in.

For each row record: notice name, trigger event, day count, calendar-vs-business-day basis, mandated wording source and delivery channel restrictions (some states forbid e-delivery without affirmative consent).
Ask Regulatory Counsel to confirm any row where the local transposition of ICP 19.5-19.9 is stricter than the group standard, and paste counsel's written answer into the row.
Publish the refreshed catalogue as Notice Catalogue v<yyyy-mm> to the compliance evidence repository and notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead by email.
checklist.done: the catalogue carries one row per notice per jurisdiction with trigger, day count, day-count basis and channel rules, dated this month.

checklist.step: Reconcile the catalogue to the trigger definitions configured in policy admin
actions: In the policy admin Configuration ▸ Correspondence ▸ Trigger Rules screen, list every active trigger with its notice code, template id and offset days.
Line the list up against the Notice Catalogue rows and mark each as Matched, Missing trigger, or Orphan trigger with no catalogue row.
Hand every Missing/Orphan row to the Configuration Engineer as a configuration defect with the catalogue reference attached.
Record the reconciliation result and the open defect ids on the monthly notice control sheet.
checklist.done: every catalogue row maps to a live trigger, and every gap is an open configuration defect with an owner.

checklist.step: Run the daily notice trigger extract
actions: Run the scheduled overnight job NOTICE_TRIGGER_EXTRACT and open the output in the Batch ▸ Job Monitor screen.
Read the control totals: triggers raised, notices queued, notices suppressed and hard errors, and compare each to the prior business day.
Open every hard error, identify the cause (missing address, null trigger date, template not effective-dated) and clear it the same day.
Export the trigger list with policy number, jurisdiction, notice code, trigger date and computed due date to the Notice Log.
checklist.done: the extract has run clean, zero hard errors remain open, and the trigger list is loaded to the Notice Log with computed due dates.

checklist.step: Reconcile triggers raised to notices actually generated
actions: Match the trigger list to the composition engine output file on policy number + notice code + trigger date.
Investigate every trigger with no rendered notice: check for suppression flags (do-not-mail, deceased, litigation hold) and confirm each suppression has a documented, permitted basis.
Escalate any suppression that is not on the permitted list to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for same-day release.
Write the matched, suppressed and unexplained counts onto the daily notice control sheet and sign it.
checklist.done: trigger count equals generated plus permitted-suppressed count, with zero unexplained gaps carried overnight.

checklist.step: Verify the template version and mandated content on each notice type
actions: Pull one rendered specimen of each notice type from OpenText Document Mgmt for the day's run.

Compare the specimen against the approved template in the forms library on: form number and edition date in the footer, mandated statutory paragraphs, the customer's rights and time limits, contact details and the complaints/ombudsman escalation wording required by ICP 19.11.
Check the merged variable fields render correctly — policy number, due date, amount due, last day of grace, effective date of lapse — against the source policy record.
Reject any specimen carrying a superseded edition date and stop that notice type's run until the Configuration Engineer republishes the template.
checklist.done: each notice type's specimen matches its approved edition and every mandated paragraph and merged field is present and correct.

checklist.step: Produce the language and accessible-format variants
actions: Filter the day's queue for policies flagged with a language preference or an accessibility need (large print, braille, audio).
Route each flagged record to the approved translated or accessible template variant, never to a machine translation of the English master.
Where a required variant does not exist, send the English master plus the approved 'language assistance available' insert and raise a content gap to Compliance the same day.
Log the variant used against the policy on the Notice Log so the delivered content can be reproduced later.
checklist.done: every flagged policy received an approved variant or the master plus assistance insert, and the variant used is recorded.

checklist.step: Dispatch through print/mail and e-delivery and capture the dispatch date
actions: Release the print stream to the outsourced print vendor by the daily 14:00 cut-off and confirm the vendor acknowledgement file returns the same piece count.
For e-delivery eligible policies, confirm an affirmative electronic-delivery consent is on file and unrevoked before suppressing paper; where consent is absent, force paper.
Record the mailing date (the vendor postmark date, not the render date) and the e-delivery send timestamp against each notice on the Notice Log.
Reconcile the vendor's nightly mail-manifest count to the released piece count and chase any variance with the vendor coordinator before the next run.
checklist.done: every notice has a dispatch channel, a postmark or send timestamp on the Notice Log, and the vendor manifest reconciles to the released count.

checklist.step: Capture proof of delivery and file the notice image
actions: Ingest the vendor's daily proof-of-mailing file and the e-delivery bounce/open receipts into the document repository, indexed by policy number and notice code.
Attach the rendered PDF image of each notice to the policy record with metadata: template id, edition date, jurisdiction, trigger date, dispatch date, channel and address used.
For certified or tracked mail (replacement and lapse notices in states that require it), file the tracking number and the carrier delivery scan.
Confirm the repository retention label 'Policy life + 7 years' is applied to the batch.
checklist.done: every dispatched notice has a filed image, indexed metadata, delivery evidence and the correct retention label.

checklist.step: Work the undeliverable and returned-mail queue
actions: Open the returned-mail queue daily and classify each item: bad address, deceased, refused, or vacant.
Run an address trace against the Credit Bureau & Data Services locator feed and, where a better address is returned, update the policy record and re-issue the notice within 2 business days.
Where no address is found, apply the unclaimed-property/lost-policyholder process and record the search attempts and dates.
Record the re-issue date on the Notice Log against the original trigger so the statutory clock is visibly re-run, not reset silently.
checklist.done: every returned item is classified, traced, re-issued or escalated to the lost-policyholder process with dated search attempts.

checklist.step: Close each Notice Log row with the day-count calculation
actions: For each dispatched notice compute elapsed days = dispatch date − trigger date, using the calendar/business-day basis recorded in the Notice Catalogue for that jurisdiction.
Compare elapsed days to the statutory window and set the row status to Within window, Late, or Not sent.
Where a jurisdiction counts from receipt rather than mailing, add the deemed-receipt days published by that regulator before comparing.
Lock the row so the computed status cannot be edited without a Compliance Officer override.
checklist.done: every Notice Log row shows elapsed days, the day-count basis used and a locked Within window / Late / Not sent status.

checklist.step: Monitor the breach queue and act the same day
actions: Open the notice aging dashboard each morning and read the three buckets: 50% of window, 80% of window and breached.
Clear the 80% bucket first by forcing the affected notices into the next print release rather than waiting for the nightly run.
For anything already breached, raise a conduct exception in the GRC platform the same business day with policy number, notice type, days late and the customer impact.
Report the breached count and reason at the daily operations stand-up and to Market Conduct weekly.
checklist.done: the 80% bucket is emptied daily and every breached row has a same-day GRC exception with a named cause.

checklist.step: Handle event-driven surges without dropping the statutory window
actions: Ahead of any known surge — mass lapse cycle, block conversion, rate change mailing, portfolio transfer — model the extra volume against the print vendor's daily capacity.
Where volume exceeds capacity, agree a phased release with the vendor that still lands every piece inside the tightest statutory window, and get the plan in writing.
Split the surge population by jurisdiction so the shortest-window states (replacement notices at 5 business days) are released first.
Brief Contact Center Ops Manager on the mailing dates and expected call volumes so customer enquiries are answered against the right notice.
checklist.done: a written phased release plan exists that keeps every jurisdiction inside its window, with the contact centre briefed on the dates.

checklist.step: Remediate a missed notice and restore the customer's position
actions: For each breach, determine the detriment: did the policy lapse, was a grace period truncated, was a replacement decision made without disclosure, was a right to complain time-barred.
Re-issue the notice with a corrected effective date and extend the customer's rights by the number of days lost, in writing.
Where a lapse occurred, reinstate without evidence of insurability and refund or waive the reinstatement interest, and record the amount.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the breach is self-reportable to the domiciliary regulator and record the decision and its basis on the exception.
checklist.done: every breach has a documented detriment assessment, a re-issued notice with extended rights, any restitution recorded and a self-report decision from counsel.

checklist.step: Report notice timeliness monthly to Market Conduct and the risk committee
actions: Build the monthly pack from the Notice Log: volume and timeliness by notice type and jurisdiction, breach count, days-late distribution, root-cause split and restitution paid.
Trend the breach rate over 13 months and call out any notice type breaching two months running as a systemic issue under ICP 19.11.
Circulate to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager by the 10th business day and table the pack at the monthly conduct risk forum.
Carry every systemic issue into the conduct risk register with an owner and a remediation date.
checklist.done: the monthly pack is issued by the 10th business day and every systemic notice type is on the conduct risk register with an owner.

checklist.step: Retain the notice and delivery evidence for the full period
actions: At month end, archive the Notice Log extract, the vendor mail manifests, the e-delivery receipt files and the template version register into the compliance evidence repository under REG-013-C17/<yyyy-mm>.
Apply the 'policy life + 7 years' retention label and confirm no legal hold is overridden by the disposal schedule.
Run a retrieval spot-check: pick 5 policies at random and confirm the notice image, template version and postmark date can be produced within 10 minutes.
Record the archive reference and the spot-check result on the monthly notice control sheet.
checklist.done: the month's evidence is archived, retention-labelled, and a 5-policy retrieval spot-check succeeded within the target time.

testing.step: Build the population of notice-triggering events for the quarter
actions: Extract from policy administration every event in the quarter that carries a notice obligation: premium due dates, grace expiries, lapses, reinstatements, replacement solicitations, underwriting declines and policy anniversaries, with policy number, writing company and jurisdiction.
Ask the Data Quality Analyst for an independent record count straight off the policy master so the extract is not self-attesting.
Reconcile the extract count to the independent count and to the in-force movement report; resolve every difference before sampling and note the resolution.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to an independent policy-master count and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the trigger population to the Notice Log
actions: Left-join the trigger population to the Notice Log on policy number + notice code + trigger date.
List every trigger with no Notice Log row as an automatic exception; suppression is only acceptable where a permitted suppression code and a documented basis are both present.
List every Notice Log row with no trigger as a second exception class — notices sent with no obligation point at a broken rule as surely as missing ones.
testing.done: every trigger is matched to a Notice Log row or listed as an exception, in both directions.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of replacement notices and 100% of grace/lapse notices in jurisdictions with a window of 10 days or shorter.
Take 40 further rows by seeded random selection stratified across notice type and jurisdiction, minimum 60 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every short-window replacement and lapse notice.

testing.step: Re-perform the statutory day-count on each sampled notice
actions: For each sampled row read the jurisdiction's day count and day-count basis straight from the Internal Regulatory System obligation record, not from the Notice Catalogue.
Recompute elapsed days = postmark or e-delivery timestamp − trigger date, applying business-day and deemed-receipt rules independently.
Compare your result to the recorded status; a right answer computed on the wrong basis still counts as an exception.
Record every recomputation on the day-count re-performance sheet with the source cite used.
testing.done: each sampled notice has an independently recomputed elapsed-day figure with its citation, agreed or exceptioned.

testing.step: Trace each sampled notice to its image, template version and delivery evidence
actions: Retrieve the rendered PDF from the document repository by policy number and notice code and confirm it is the notice claimed, not a generic reprint.
Read the form number and edition date from the footer and confirm it was the approved edition on the dispatch date, using the forms library version history.
Confirm the proof of mailing (vendor manifest line or carrier scan) or the e-delivery receipt exists and carries the dispatch date recorded on the Notice Log.
Screenshot the repository metadata panel into the workpaper as the trace evidence.
testing.done: every sampled notice traces to an image on the then-current edition with matching, dated delivery evidence.

testing.step: Re-perform the content test against the mandated wording
actions: For 15 sampled notices spanning every notice type, read the delivered image against the statutory wording in the Internal Regulatory System obligation record.

Confirm the mandated elements are present and legible: the customer's right and the deadline to exercise it, the amount and date, the consequence of inaction, and the complaints escalation route required by ICP 19.11.
Check merged fields against the policy record — a correct template with a wrong grace-expiry date is a content failure, not a cosmetic one.
Mark any omission or wrong merged value as a fail and note which element was missing.
testing.done: each of the 15 content-tested notices is confirmed complete against the mandated wording, or the missing element is named.

testing.step: Test the e-delivery consent behind every suppressed paper notice
actions: Filter the sample to notices delivered electronically and pull the consent record for each policy.
Confirm the consent is affirmative, specific to the notice types delivered, dated before the dispatch, and not revoked as at the dispatch date.
Confirm a bounce or non-open on a short-window notice triggered a paper re-issue inside the remaining window.
Treat implied or bundled consent as a fail.
testing.done: every electronically delivered sampled notice has a dated, unrevoked affirmative consent and bounce handling evidence.

testing.step: Test the returned-mail and re-issue path end to end
actions: Pull the quarter's returned-mail queue and select 15 items across bad address, deceased and refused classifications.
For each, confirm an address trace was run, the outcome recorded, and — where a new address was found — the notice re-issued within 2 business days.
Confirm the re-issue is logged against the original trigger with a fresh dispatch date rather than closing the original row as delivered.
Confirm no-trace items entered the lost-policyholder process with dated search attempts.
testing.done: each sampled returned item shows a trace, an outcome and either a dated re-issue or entry into the lost-policyholder process.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception with policy number, notice type, jurisdiction, days late and customer detriment.
Assign a root cause from the fixed taxonomy — trigger not configured, template superseded, print capacity, address quality, wrong day-count basis, improper suppression — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, where detriment occurred, confirm restitution and rights extension were completed and evidenced.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a taxonomy root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute timeliness by notice type against the thresholds — 100% for replacement and grace/lapse, 99.5% elsewhere — and state pass or fail per type.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who operated none of the notice runs and approved none of the sampled templates, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any self-reportable breaches to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-013-C17.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-notice-type pass rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

In-scope processes.value: Regulatory change intake → requirement specification → configuration build → QA and regression → CAB approval → effective-dated production release, for every correspondence trigger rule, offset table, suppression rule and notice template

In-scope systems.value: Configuration ▸ Correspondence trigger rules and offset tables in policy admin; templates in the composition engine; code and config versioned in Azure DevOps; change records raised in the ITSM platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Notice Configuration Change Procedure NCC-02 — requirement-to-rule traceability matrix, effective-dating standard (never retro-date a live rule), mandatory boundary test cases for each day count, and the four-eyes build/review split

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Head of IT and the Compliance Manager; re-approved on every major policy-admin platform upgrade and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the configuration must be live in production on or before the regulatory effective date of the rule it implements; the release plan works back from that date with a 10-business-day QA and regression window and a 5-business-day CAB lead time

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every regulatory change record in the ITSM platform carries the rule's effective date as its due date, with alerts at 60, 30 and 10 business days out to the Configuration Engineer and the Compliance Analyst

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any configuration deployed without a linked requirement, without evidenced testing, or after the regulatory effective date is logged as a change-control exception with the notice population affected and a back-out or catch-up disposition

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All correspondence configuration releases deployed to production in the half-year — trigger rules, offset tables, suppression rules and template versions — taken from the Azure DevOps release history rather than the change tickets

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have no build access to the correspondence configuration and must not have authored any sampled change

checklist.step: Take the regulatory change into the configuration intake queue
actions: Open the regulatory change alert from Compliance and raise a change record of type 'Regulatory — correspondence' in the ITSM platform.

Copy onto the record: the obligation id from the Internal Regulatory System, the jurisdiction, the regulatory effective date, and whether the change alters a day count, a content block, a trigger condition or a suppression rule.
Ask the Compliance Analyst for the source text extract and the counsel interpretation, and attach both to the record — never work from a summary email.
Set the record due date to the regulatory effective date minus the 15-business-day build-test-CAB window.
checklist.done: a change record exists with the obligation id, source text, counsel interpretation and a due date backed off the regulatory effective date.

checklist.step: Write the requirement specification down to field level
actions: Write one requirement line per rule element: trigger event and its source field in policy admin, offset days, calendar-vs-business-day basis, holiday calendar used, deemed-receipt days, and the suppression conditions that are permitted.
For content changes, specify the exact mandated paragraph text, its placement in the template, and the merged fields it depends on.

State the effective-dating rule explicitly: the new configuration applies to triggers dated on or after the regulatory effective date, and the superseded rule stays available for reprints of earlier notices.
Have the Compliance Analyst sign the specification line by line against the source text before any build starts.
checklist.done: every rule element has a signed requirement line with trigger field, offset, day basis, holiday calendar and effective-dating instruction.

checklist.step: Impact-assess every configuration object the change touches
actions: Search the correspondence configuration for every rule, offset table row, template and suppression condition referencing the affected notice code or jurisdiction.
List downstream dependencies: the composition engine template, the print vendor mapping file, the Notice Log field layout and any reporting extract that reads the notice code.
Identify shared objects used by other jurisdictions and flag them — a shared offset table changed for one state silently changes fifty.
Publish the impact list on the change record and get the Policy Admin Ops Lead to confirm the operational blast radius.
checklist.done: the change record carries a complete object and dependency list, with shared objects flagged and the operational impact confirmed.

checklist.step: Build the configuration in the development environment
actions: Branch the configuration in Azure DevOps as feature/REG-013-C18-<change id> so every edit is diffable.
In Configuration ▸ Correspondence ▸ Trigger Rules create a new effective-dated version of the rule rather than editing the live one, and set its start date to the regulatory effective date.
Populate the offset table row with the day count, the day-count basis flag and the holiday calendar id specified in the requirement.
Where the requirement adds a permitted suppression, code it as an explicit whitelist condition — never as a catch-all exclusion.
Commit with the change record id in the commit message so the build is traceable both ways.
checklist.done: an effective-dated rule version exists on a named branch with the specified offset, basis and holiday calendar, committed against the change id.

checklist.step: Update the notice template and its variable data mapping
actions: Open the notice template in the composition engine, insert or amend the mandated paragraph exactly as specified, and increment the edition date in the footer.
Map each new merged field to its policy-admin source attribute and set a hard fail — not a blank — where the source is null, so an incomplete notice cannot render.
Regenerate the translated and accessible variants of the template so the variants do not drift from the master edition.
Publish the template to the QA environment only, and record the new template id and edition date on the change record.
checklist.done: the template carries the new edition date, the mandated text, null-safe field mappings and regenerated variants, published to QA only.

checklist.step: Peer review the configuration against the requirement line by line
actions: Open the pull request and read the configuration diff against the signed requirement, ticking each requirement line as met or not met.
Check the effective-date field on every changed object and reject any object whose start date is in the past.
Confirm no shared object was edited in place where the impact list said other jurisdictions depend on it.
Record the review outcome in the pull request; the builder may not approve their own pull request.
checklist.done: the pull request carries a line-by-line reviewer tick-off by someone other than the builder, with no past-dated effective dates.

checklist.step: Write the boundary test cases the day-count rule must survive
actions: Write one test case per boundary: trigger on the regulatory effective date itself, trigger the day before, trigger on a weekend, trigger on a public holiday in the jurisdiction's calendar, and a leap-day trigger.
Add a deemed-receipt case for every jurisdiction that counts from receipt, and a case where the customer's e-delivery consent is revoked mid-window.
For each case state the expected dispatch date computed by hand from the statute, not from the system.
Load the cases into the test plan linked to the change record so coverage is provable.
checklist.done: the test plan holds effective-date, weekend, holiday, leap-day, deemed-receipt and consent-revocation cases with hand-computed expected dates.

checklist.step: Execute the test cases in the QA environment
actions: Seed QA policies matching each test case and run the notice trigger batch with the system date set to the case date.
Compare the generated dispatch date and the rendered template edition to the hand-computed expected result, field by field.
Open each rendered PDF and confirm the mandated paragraph appears in the specified position with correct merged values.
Attach the evidence — screenshots, rendered PDFs and the pass/fail grid — to the change record and fail the build on any single mismatch.
checklist.done: every boundary case has an executed result, an attached rendered PDF and a pass verdict, with no mismatch outstanding.

checklist.step: Run regression across the notice types the change did not intend to touch
actions: Run the correspondence regression suite covering every active notice code across all jurisdictions in the QA environment.
Diff the regression output dispatch dates and template ids against the prior baseline run and investigate every difference.
Pay particular attention to notice codes sharing the offset table or template fragments listed on the impact assessment.
Publish the regression report to the change record and block promotion while any unexplained difference stands.
checklist.done: the regression suite has run green, with every difference from baseline either intended and documented or resolved.

checklist.step: Run user acceptance with Policy Administration and Compliance
actions: Walk the Compliance Analyst through the rendered notices for each affected jurisdiction and have them confirm the wording matches the source text.
Have a Policy Administration Analyst run a day in the life — trigger, generate, suppress, reissue — and confirm the operational queues behave.
Capture both sign-offs on the change record with names and dates; a verbal acceptance is not an acceptance.
Record any accepted-with-conditions item as a follow-up ticket with a due date before the regulatory effective date.
checklist.done: dated UAT sign-offs from Policy Administration and Compliance are on the change record, with conditions ticketed and dated.

checklist.step: Take the change through CAB with the regulatory driver stated
actions: Complete the change record: regulatory driver and effective date, objects changed, test and regression evidence links, back-out plan and the notice population affected if the change fails.
Present at CAB at least 5 business days before the target release and confirm the release date lands on or before the regulatory effective date.
Obtain CAB approval from an approver who is neither the builder nor the reviewer, and record it on the record.
Where CAB cannot clear the change in time, raise a compliance exception immediately rather than releasing unapproved.
checklist.done: CAB has approved the change on the record, by an approver independent of build and review, with the release date inside the regulatory deadline.

checklist.step: Deploy to production with the effective dating intact
actions: Promote the approved branch through the pipeline; confirm the pipeline enforces that the deployer is not the committer.
After deployment, open the production Configuration ▸ Correspondence screen and read back the rule version, its start date and the offset table row.
Confirm the superseded rule version remains present and end-dated so historic notices can still be reproduced on the rule that generated them.
Record the deployment timestamp, build number and deployer on the change record.
checklist.done: the new rule version is live in production with the correct start date, the superseded version is end-dated, and the deployment is recorded.

checklist.step: Verify the first live notice run after the change
actions: On the first business day after the effective date, pull the notice trigger extract and filter to the affected notice code and jurisdiction.
Take 10 live notices, recompute the dispatch date by hand and open the rendered PDF to confirm the new edition and wording.
Compare the day's volume to the prior week's average — a sudden drop usually means a suppression rule swallowed the population.
Post the verification result to the change record and close it only when the 10 checks pass.
checklist.done: 10 live notices verified by hand against the new rule with volumes in line, and the change record closed on that evidence.

checklist.step: Update the traceability matrix and the configuration register
actions: Add or update the matrix row: obligation id, jurisdiction, statutory day count and content requirement, rule id, offset table row, template id and edition, effective date and change record id.
End-date the superseded matrix row rather than deleting it, so the matrix can answer 'what was live on this date' for an examiner.
Circulate the updated matrix to Compliance and Internal Audit and store the version in the compliance evidence repository.
Flag any obligation row still without a rule id as an open configuration gap on the compliance risk register.
checklist.done: the matrix shows a current and an end-dated row per obligation with rule, template and effective date, and open gaps are on the risk register.

checklist.step: Archive the configuration evidence package
actions: Bundle the requirement spec, configuration diff, pull-request review, test plan and results, regression report, UAT sign-offs, CAB approval and post-implementation verification into one package named REG-013-C18/<change id>.
Apply the 7-years-from-configuration-retirement retention label to the package.
Confirm the package is indexed and searchable by obligation id, jurisdiction, rule id and effective date.
Record the archive reference on the change record before it is closed.
checklist.done: a single indexed evidence package per change exists, retention-labelled, referenced from the closed change record.

testing.step: Build the population of correspondence configuration releases
actions: Extract every production deployment in the half-year touching the correspondence configuration path — trigger rules, offset tables, suppression rules, templates — from the Azure DevOps release history.
Take the extract from the pipeline, not from the ITSM change list, so changes deployed without a ticket cannot hide.
Reconcile deployment count to the pipeline run log and to the policy-admin configuration version history, and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the release population is built from pipeline history and reconciled to the platform's own version history.

testing.step: Reconcile every release to an approved change record
actions: Match each deployment to an ITSM change record on change id in the commit message.
List every deployment with no change record, or with a record approved after the deployment timestamp, as an automatic exception.
List every change record whose linked obligation id is blank as a second exception class — a correspondence rule with no obligation behind it is unsupported.
testing.done: every deployment is matched to a pre-approved change record with a populated obligation id, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of releases
actions: Take 100% of releases that changed a day-count offset or a mandated content block.
Take 15 further releases by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 25 releases in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every day-count and mandated-content release.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement-to-rule trace on each sampled release
actions: Open the obligation record in the Internal Regulatory System and read the statutory day count and content requirement from the source text.
Open the live rule in policy admin Configuration ▸ Correspondence and read the offset days, day-count basis and holiday calendar without looking at the requirement spec first.
Compare your reading to the configuration; a mismatch in the day-count basis (calendar vs business days) counts as a full failure even where the number matches.
Screenshot both the obligation record and the configuration screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled rule has an independent source-to-configuration comparison with both screens captured.

testing.step: Re-execute the boundary cases in a controlled environment
actions: In the QA environment refreshed from production configuration, seed policies for the weekend, public-holiday, effective-date-boundary and leap-day cases for each sampled rule.
Run the notice trigger batch with the system date set to each case date and read the computed dispatch date.
Compare to the date you compute by hand from the statute; do not reuse the project's original expected results.
Record every case and verdict on the re-execution grid in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled rule has independently re-executed boundary cases with hand-computed expected dates and a recorded verdict.

testing.step: Test effective dating and the reproducibility of superseded rules
actions: For each sampled rule read the start date of the live version and confirm it is on or before the regulatory effective date on the obligation record.
Confirm the superseded version is present and end-dated, then reprint one notice generated under the old rule and confirm it renders on the old edition.
Flag any rule edited in place, any past-dated start date and any superseded version that has been deleted.
Compute days late where a rule went live after its regulatory effective date and record the notice population issued in the gap.
testing.done: effective dates reconcile to the obligation records, superseded versions reprint correctly, and any late-live period is quantified by population.

testing.step: Test segregation of duties across build, review, approval and deployment
actions: For each sampled release list the committer, the pull-request approver, the CAB approver and the deployer from the pipeline and ITSM records.
Flag any release where two of those four roles are the same person.
Pull the correspondence configuration write-access group from the IAM platform and confirm every member has a current, approved entitlement.
Flag standing production write access held by anyone outside the Configuration Engineer group.
testing.done: no sampled release has overlapping build/review/approve/deploy identities, and production write access is confined to approved entitlements.

testing.step: Test the evidence completeness of each sampled change package
actions: Retrieve the archived package for each sampled release and check for the seven mandatory artefacts: requirement spec, diff, review, test results, regression report, UAT sign-off and CAB approval.
Confirm the UAT sign-off names an individual with a date, not a team mailbox.
Confirm the post-implementation verification recorded 10 live notices with hand-computed dates.
Compute the evidence-gap rate across the sample against the 5% threshold.
testing.done: each sampled package is checked against the seven mandatory artefacts and the evidence-gap rate is computed against the threshold.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the release id, rule id, obligation id and the notice population exposed while the defective configuration was live.
Assign a root cause from the taxonomy — no requirement, wrong day-count basis, in-place edit, missing effective date, testing skipped, SoD breach, late to effective date — and an accountable owner.
Where notices were generated on a wrong rule, open a linked remediation to re-issue those notices and extend the affected customers' rights.
Set a remediation date and carry every open issue into the next half-year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a quantified notice exposure, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State pass or fail against each zero-tolerance item — unlinked release, late-to-effective-date rule, self-approved deployment — and against the 5% evidence-gap threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no build access to the correspondence configuration and authored no sampled change, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and to the Head of IT at the next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-013-C18.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-threshold verdicts, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Define the in-scope audience and map roles to curricula
actions: Pull the active roster from Workday HCM with job profile, cost centre, legal entity, country and manager for every employee, fixed-term worker and long-term contractor.

Map each job profile to one of the ICP curricula — AML/CFT and sanctions (ICP 22), fair treatment and complaints (ICP 19), investment and derivatives controls (ICP 15), governance and internal controls (ICP 8) — and record the mapping rationale.
Send the mapping to each business-unit HR Business Partner for confirmation that no client-facing or control-function profile has been left unmapped.
Publish the confirmed role-to-curriculum matrix as the audience definition for the cycle and store it in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every active job profile carries a confirmed curriculum assignment or a documented out-of-scope rationale.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum against the current ICP text and local rules
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System, filter obligations to regCode REG-013, and list every obligation whose text changed since the last cycle.

For each changed obligation identify the module and slide that teaches it and mark it for rewrite, quoting the new standard reference (for example ICP 22 Standard 22.3 on proportionate enhanced and simplified measures).
Add the year's actual incidents — complaint themes, audit findings, near misses, sanctions screening errors — as worked examples so the course teaches from the firm's own failures.
Publish the change log listing every module amended and the obligation driving it.
checklist.done: a change log names every amended module with the obligation reference and incident examples behind the amendment.

checklist.step: Build the course content and the role-specific scenarios
actions: Author each module to the change log, keeping the core to 25 minutes and the role-specific branch to 15 minutes.

Write branch scenarios that match the job: a customer-due-diligence escalation for the AML branch, a grace-period notice decision for policy administration, a complaint root-cause call for the complaints branch, a derivatives limit breach for investment operations.
Include the escalation route and the named internal contact for each scenario so the learner leaves knowing who to call.
Meet the accessibility standard — captions, transcripts, keyboard navigation — and produce the local-language versions required in each operating country.
checklist.done: each curriculum has an authored core, a role-specific branch with realistic scenarios, accessibility features and required language versions.

checklist.step: Get subject-matter and legal approval on the content
actions: Review each module against the cited ICP standard and the local transposing rule and mark any statement that overstates or understates the obligation.
Confirm the worked examples describe the firm's actual approved procedure, not an idealised one, so training and procedure cannot diverge.
Return comments within 10 business days and re-review the amended deck before release.
Issue a dated approval memo naming the curriculum version approved and file it with the course record.
checklist.done: a dated counsel approval memo exists naming the approved curriculum version, with all comments closed.

checklist.step: Build the assessment and set the pass rules
actions: Write a 15-question assessment per curriculum with at least 6 scenario-based questions that require a judgement, not a recall.
Set the pass mark at 80%, allow two retakes, and configure a third failure to route the learner to a live session with a Trainer rather than an endless retake loop.
Randomise question order and draw from a bank of at least 40 questions so answers cannot be shared across the cohort.
Pilot the assessment with 10 staff across the affected roles and adjust any question with a pass rate above 98% or below 40%.
checklist.done: each assessment is piloted, drawn from a randomised bank, with an 80% pass mark and a defined third-failure path.

checklist.step: Configure the LMS curricula, audiences and due dates
actions: Create the curriculum objects for the cycle year and attach the approved content version and assessment.
Build dynamic audience rules from the role-to-curriculum matrix using Workday job profile, legal entity and country attributes so assignment follows the person, not a static list.
Set the cycle due date to 31 May and configure a rolling 30-calendar-day due date for anyone entering the audience mid-cycle.
Configure reminders at 30, 14, 7 and 1 days and the Monday manager exception report from day 15.
checklist.done: curricula are live with dynamic audience rules, a 31 May cycle date, a rolling 30-day joiner rule and the reminder schedule configured.

checklist.step: Prove the nightly HRIS-to-LMS audience feed is complete
actions: Compare the Workday active headcount by legal entity against the LMS assigned-learner count for the same entities each week during the cycle.
Investigate every variance: leavers not yet removed, joiners not yet fed, contractors held outside HRIS, job profiles added since the matrix was built.
Raise a data ticket for any population held outside HRIS and agree a manual assignment route with the Learning Development Manager until it is fixed.
Record the weekly reconciliation result and the unresolved variance count on the training control sheet.
checklist.done: the weekly HRIS-to-LMS variance is explained to zero or carried as a named, ticketed population with a manual assignment.

checklist.step: Launch the cycle and communicate the consequence of non-completion
actions: Send the launch communication on 1 March from the Head of Compliance stating the 31 May deadline, what changed this year and why.
State plainly the consequence of non-completion: manager escalation from day 15, Head of Compliance list at day 0, and system access restriction for control-function and AML-facing roles.
Brief the business-unit leadership team at their operating meetings so managers own their own delinquency numbers.
Publish the completion dashboard link so every manager can see their team's position daily.
checklist.done: the cycle is launched with a dated communication, stated consequences, briefed managers and a live completion dashboard.

checklist.step: Deliver the live sessions for high-risk and hard-to-reach roles
actions: Schedule facilitated sessions for AML-facing, complaints-handling and control-function staff where an e-learning module alone will not evidence competence.
Run each session against the approved deck, capture the attendee list from the meeting register, and record attendance in the LMS the same day.
Capture the questions asked and feed recurring confusion back to the Instructional Designer as content defects.
Run catch-up sessions for shift and field staff outside core hours so the population is genuinely reachable.
checklist.done: every high-risk role has an attended live session recorded in the LMS, with recurring questions logged as content defects.

checklist.step: Track completion weekly and work the delinquency ladder
actions: Publish the Monday completion report by business unit, curriculum and manager, showing completed, in progress and not started.
From day 15 escalate not-started learners to their line manager; from day 30 escalate to the business-unit head; at cycle close escalate the remaining list to the Head of Compliance.
Track assessment failures separately and route third-failure learners to a live session within 10 business days.
Record each escalation step and date against the learner so the ladder is evidenced, not asserted.
checklist.done: a dated escalation trail exists for every delinquent learner through manager, business-unit head and Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Apply and evidence the exemption and leave rules
actions: Pull the Workday leave register for the cycle and identify learners on maternity, parental, long-term sick or sabbatical leave covering the due date.
Defer those learners with a new due date of 30 calendar days after their recorded return-to-work date — never waive.
Record the deferral reason, the leave dates and the new due date against the learner record so the deferral is auditable.
Refuse any exemption request based on workload or seniority and escalate the requester to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every deferral is tied to a Workday leave record with a return-based new due date, and no workload-based exemption exists.

checklist.step: Capture the learner attestation with the completion
actions: Configure the course to require a typed attestation before the completion is recorded: that the learner understands the obligations covered and will escalate suspected breaches through the named route.
Store the attestation text version alongside the completion so the wording the learner signed can be reproduced.
For live sessions, collect the attestation on the signed attendance sheet and scan it to the learner record within 2 business days.
Reject any completion recorded without an attestation and reopen the assignment.
checklist.done: every completion, e-learning or live, carries a stored attestation with its version and date.

checklist.step: Feed complaints, audit and incident findings back into the curriculum
actions: Each quarter pull the GRC issue list for complaint root causes, audit findings and near misses tagged to REG-013 obligations.
Identify findings whose root cause is 'staff did not know the requirement' and raise a content change request against the relevant module.
Where the finding cannot wait for the annual cycle, commission a targeted 10-minute refresher with a 30-day due date for the affected team only.
Record the link between the finding id and the training change on the GRC issue so the remediation is evidenced.
checklist.done: every knowledge-driven finding is linked to either an annual content change or a targeted refresher with a due date.

checklist.step: Report cycle outcomes to the Compliance Committee
actions: Build the June pack: completion rate by business unit and curriculum against the 98% general and 100% control-function thresholds, assessment pass rates, retake volumes and open delinquents by name.
Present the access restrictions applied and the performance file notes raised, so the consequence is visible to the committee.
Table the content change log and the counsel approval memo as evidence the curriculum tracked the ICP text.
Record the committee's decision on any residual delinquency and the deadline it sets.
checklist.done: the June committee pack is tabled with completion against thresholds, consequences applied and a recorded committee decision on residuals.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle evidence
actions: Archive the audience matrix, curriculum version and content files, counsel approval memo, assessment bank, completion register, attestation extract and escalation trail under REG-013-C19/<cycle year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-completion retention label and confirm the leaver records are retained despite the HRIS purge schedule.
Spot-check retrieval for 5 learners including one leaver, confirming completion date, score and attestation can be produced within 10 minutes.
Record the archive reference on the training control sheet.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence is archived and retention-labelled, with a 5-learner retrieval spot-check including a leaver.

testing.step: Build the population of learners who should have been trained
actions: Extract from Workday every worker active at any point in the cycle with job profile, entity, country, start date, role-change dates and leave dates.
Add the contractor and third-party administrator populations held outside HRIS from the vendor register, since ICP-relevant work is performed there too.
Apply the role-to-curriculum matrix independently to derive who should have been assigned, and reconcile your derived population to headcount reports signed by each business unit.
testing.done: an independently derived in-scope learner population exists, reconciled to business-unit headcount and including outsourced staff.

testing.step: Reconcile the derived population to LMS assignments
actions: Extract the LMS assignment list for the cycle and left-join the derived population to it on employee id.
List every in-scope worker with no assignment as an automatic exception and identify whether the audience rule, the HRIS feed or the matrix caused the miss.
List every assignment with no in-scope worker as a second exception class — assigning leavers inflates the denominator and hides real gaps.
testing.done: every in-scope worker is matched to an assignment or exceptioned, with the cause of each miss identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of learners
actions: Take 100% of control-function, AML-facing and complaints-handling learners, and 100% of joiners and role changes in the cycle.
Take 45 further learners by seeded random selection stratified across business unit and country, minimum 75 in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every high-risk role plus all joiners and role changes.

testing.step: Re-perform the completion and score check on each sampled learner
actions: Open each sampled learner's transcript and read the completion date, the assessment score, the attempt count and the content version taken.
Confirm the score is at or above the 80% pass mark and that a third failure routed to a live session rather than being marked complete.
Confirm the content version taken is the counsel-approved version for the cycle, not a prior-year carry-over.
Capture the transcript screen into the workpaper for each sampled learner.
testing.done: each sampled learner's completion, score, attempts and content version are verified from the transcript and captured.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day new-joiner and role-change clocks
actions: For every joiner and role change in the sample, recompute due date = start or role-change effective date + 30 calendar days from the Workday record, not the LMS due-date field.
Compare the LMS completion date to your recomputed due date and count days late where it falls after.
Check the LMS due date itself against your recomputation — a wrong system due date makes on-time completions illusory.
Record every recomputation on the day-count sheet with the Workday source dates.
testing.done: each joiner and role change has an independently recomputed 30-day due date, compared to both the LMS due date and the completion date.

testing.step: Test the content currency against the regulatory text
actions: List every REG-013 obligation whose text changed in the year from the Internal Regulatory System version history.
For each, open the delivered course version and confirm the module teaches the current requirement, quoting the ICP standard reference used in the slide.
Confirm the counsel approval memo pre-dates the cycle launch and names the version actually delivered.
Treat a module still teaching a superseded day count or threshold as a content failure regardless of completion rates.
testing.done: every changed obligation is traced to a current module in the delivered version, with the counsel memo pre-dating launch.

testing.step: Test the escalation ladder actually operated
actions: Select 20 learners who were past due at any point in the cycle from the LMS delinquency history.
For each, look for the dated day-15 manager escalation, the day-30 business-unit escalation and the cycle-close Head of Compliance listing.
For control-function and AML-facing delinquents, confirm the system access restriction was actually applied by checking the IAM platform entitlement change record.
Flag any delinquent whose escalation stopped at an email with no recorded consequence.
testing.done: each of the 20 delinquents shows a dated escalation at every rung, with access restrictions evidenced in the IAM record where required.

testing.step: Test the deferral and exemption population
actions: Extract every deferral recorded in the cycle and match each to a Workday leave record covering the original due date.
Recompute the new due date as return-to-work date + 30 calendar days and confirm the learner completed by it.
Flag any deferral without a leave record, any waiver rather than deferral, and any deferral granted to a control-function learner.
Compute the deferral rate by business unit and flag any unit materially above the group average for root-cause enquiry.
testing.done: every deferral is supported by a leave record with a recomputed return-based due date, and waivers are identified as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception naming the learner population, the business unit and the control impact — an untrained AML-facing team is a live financial-crime exposure, not a paperwork gap.
Assign a root cause from the taxonomy — audience rule gap, HRIS feed failure, matrix mapping missing, delinquency not escalated, unsupported deferral, stale content — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and require completion evidence, not a promise, for every untrained in-scope learner.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a taxonomy root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute completion against the 98% general and 100% control-function thresholds using your derived population, not the LMS denominator.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective), stating explicitly whether the denominator itself was reliable.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance and Learning & Development and holds no LMS administration rights, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Compliance Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper under REG-013-C19.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating completion against thresholds on an audited denominator, with a conclusion and committee reporting date, exists in the repository.
