checklist.step: Derive the filing matrix from the legal entity register
actions: Pull every insurance legal entity with its domicile, licence status, group membership and whether it is part of an insurance holding company system.
For each entity list the governance disclosures its domicile requires — CGAD, Form B, Form F, ORSA summary, and in Europe the RSR and SFCR — and the statutory due date for each.
Determine and record the lead state for the group, since the CGAD is filed with the lead state and not with every domicile, and note the states that require a separate copy.
Circulate the matrix to the Corporate Secretary and the Regulatory Filing Specialist for confirmation and load each row into the filing calendar.
checklist.done: a confirmed matrix exists with one row per entity per form per jurisdiction, a determined lead state, and every row loaded to the calendar.

checklist.step: Re-read the current instructions for each form before drafting
actions: Open the lead state's CGAD instructions and the domiciliary Form B and Form F instructions for the current year and read them in full — content requirements and signature blocks change between cycles.
Check for state bulletins issued since the last cycle that alter a due date, an exhibit, a filing channel or the confidentiality treatment.
Print each instruction set to PDF named <state>-<form>-instructions-<yyyy>.pdf and file it as the evidence behind the content plan.
Where the instructions are ambiguous, email the state's designated contact and record the question, date and answer in the filing file.
checklist.done: a dated instruction capture exists per form per state, with any ambiguity resolved in writing by the regulator.

checklist.step: Issue the content request against a source map
actions: Build the content-to-source map: each CGAD assertion — board structure and committees, director independence, board practices and meeting frequency, policies on remuneration, succession and conflicts, oversight of the control functions — mapped to the charter, register entry or minute that evidences it.

Issue the content request at T-90 to the named owners: Board Governance Lead for structure and evaluation, Chief HR Officer for remuneration, Chief Risk Officer for risk oversight, Chief Audit Executive for internal audit oversight.
State for each owner exactly which assertion they are supporting and which source document must be cited, so the return is evidence rather than prose.
Track returns against the T-45 draft milestone and escalate any owner two weeks late to the General Counsel.
checklist.done: every CGAD assertion has a named owner, a required source citation and a tracked return against the T-45 milestone.

checklist.step: Draft the CGAD
actions: Draft to the lead state's prescribed structure, choosing and stating the level at which the disclosure is made — ultimate controlling person, intermediate holding company or insurer — and keeping that level consistent with the prior year unless a change is explained.

Describe the board and committee structure exactly as it stood at the reporting date, with membership numbers, independence counts, meeting frequency and the qualifications the board collectively holds.
Describe the policies actually in force for nomination, succession, remuneration, conflicts and control-function oversight, citing the approving resolution for each.
Where the structure changed during the year, describe the change and its date rather than presenting only the year-end position.
checklist.done: a complete CGAD draft exists at a stated disclosure level, with structure, membership, policies and in-year changes each tied to a cited source.

checklist.step: Assemble the holding-company registration statement and enterprise risk report
actions: Build the Form B: the organisational chart with ownership percentages, the ultimate controlling person, directors and officers of the insurer and of the controlling entities, and every affiliate agreement in force with its terms.
Reconcile the organisational chart to the legal entity register and to the equity ownership schedules in the statutory annual statement so the three cannot disagree.

Build the Form F enterprise risk report covering material developments in the group's risk profile, strategy changes, affiliate transactions of a material nature and any regulatory or credit events affecting the group.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm the Form F risk narrative agrees with the current ORSA and the board-approved risk appetite.
checklist.done: Form B ties to the entity register and annual statement schedules, and Form F carries a Chief Risk Officer confirmation that it agrees with the ORSA.

checklist.step: Align the ORSA summary report with the governance disclosures
actions: Confirm the ORSA summary report's description of the risk management framework and board oversight matches what the CGAD and Form F assert.
Confirm the board's review and approval of the ORSA is minuted, with the meeting date and resolution reference available to cite.
Agree the ORSA filing date with the lead state and load it into the filing calendar alongside the CGAD and Form B dates.
Record any inconsistency found between the three documents and resolve it before any of them is filed.
checklist.done: the ORSA, CGAD and Form F tell the same story about board oversight, with the board approval minuted and the filing date agreed with the lead state.

checklist.step: Reconcile every disclosed statement to its source
actions: Work through the draft line by line and record on the reconciliation sheet the source document, its date and the specific clause or minute reference behind each factual statement.
Check every number — committee sizes, independent-member counts, meeting counts, attendance rates — against the composition register and the attendance record rather than the prior year's filing.
Flag any statement that survives only because it was in last year's filing and cannot be sourced this year.
Have the Corporate Secretary sign the reconciliation sheet before legal review.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation sheet cites a dated source for every factual statement and number in the draft.

checklist.step: Take the draft through legal review and the confidentiality assertion
actions: Review the draft against the form instructions for completeness and against the reconciliation for accuracy, and mark any statement that overstates the maturity of a governance practice.
Prepare the confidentiality assertion in the form the state requires, since CGAD content is treated as confidential and proprietary in most states, and check the state's mechanism for claiming it.
Confirm nothing in the draft contradicts a published document — the annual report, the SFCR, a rating agency submission or a prior filing.
Clear the draft for certification within the T-21 milestone and record the clearance in the filing file.
checklist.done: legal review is closed by T-21 with the confidentiality assertion prepared in the state's required form and no contradiction with published documents.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer certification and any board approval
actions: Read the certification wording the form requires — typically a signed statement by the chief executive or corporate secretary that the disclosure has been prepared consistently with the model act and delivered to the board or an appropriate committee.
Confirm the board or the designated committee has actually received the disclosure and that receipt is minuted, since the certification asserts it.
Sign the certification at the T-10 milestone with the date, and refuse to sign where the reconciliation sheet is incomplete.
File the signed certification with the draft in the filing file.
checklist.done: a dated officer certification is signed against a complete reconciliation, with board or committee receipt minuted.

checklist.step: Submit the filings through the correct channel and capture confirmations
actions: Submit the CGAD to the lead state through the channel its instructions specify and the Form B and Form F to each domiciliary regulator, using the NAIC iSite+ or state portal route as directed.
Submit at least 3 business days before the statutory due date so a portal rejection can be corrected inside the deadline.
Capture the submission confirmation, the tracking or receipt reference and the timestamp for each filing and attach them to the filing calendar row.
Confirm the filing shows as received on the regulator's side and chase any that does not within one business day.
checklist.done: every filing is submitted at least 3 business days early with a captured confirmation reference and a verified received status.

checklist.step: Run the event-driven filing triggers continuously
actions: Monitor the trigger list weekly: any change of control or acquisition of 10% or more of voting securities (Form A, required before completion), any material affiliate transaction (Form D, filed at least 30 days before the transaction), any officer or director change (notification within 30 days), and any material change to the group structure.
Take the trigger feed from Corporate Development, Treasury and the Corporate Secretary rather than waiting to be told, and record the event date the moment it is known.
Compute the filing deadline from the event date and open a tracker row with the owner and the form required.
Escalate immediately to General Counsel where a transaction is scheduled to complete before the required prior filing can be made.
checklist.done: every trigger event is captured within a week with a computed deadline, an owner and a tracker row, and prior-filing conflicts are escalated.

checklist.step: Handle regulator questions and amended filings
actions: Log every regulator question on a filing with the date received, the deadline given and the owner, and acknowledge within 2 business days.
Draft the response against the same reconciliation sheet used for the filing so the answer cannot drift from the filed position.
Where an error is found, prepare an amended filing rather than answering informally, and have General Counsel clear the covering explanation.
Record the response, the amended filing and the regulator's closure in the filing file.
checklist.done: every regulator question is logged, answered inside its deadline from the original reconciliation, and any error corrected by an amended filing.

checklist.step: Report the filing position to the board
actions: Table a filing status paper at the board meeting nearest 1 June listing every governance disclosure due, its status, its filing date and any late or amended filing.
Present the CGAD as filed so the board can see the assertions made about its own practices, since the certification says the board received it.
Record the board's confirmation of receipt in the minutes with the meeting date, and cite that minute in next year's certification.
Report any exception and its remediation to the audit committee.
checklist.done: the board has received the filed CGAD with a minuted confirmation, and the filing status including exceptions is tabled.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed set to the calendar and close the cycle
actions: After the deadline, tick every calendar row against a captured submission confirmation and list any row with no confirmation.
Compute days early or late for each filing against its statutory due date and record the figure on the row.
Raise a tracker exception for every missing or late filing with the entity, form, days late and the corrective action.
Close the cycle with a signed statement that every required filing has been made, or that the exceptions listed are the complete set.
checklist.done: every calendar row is closed against a confirmation, days early or late are computed, and a signed cycle-completion statement exists.

checklist.step: Archive the filed set and its support
actions: Archive per entity per form: the instructions capture, the draft history, the reconciliation sheet, the legal clearance, the signed certification, the filed document as submitted, the submission confirmation and all regulator correspondence, under REG-013-C23/<entity>/<year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-filing retention label and mark the CGAD content as confidential in line with the state's treatment.
Confirm the archive is searchable by entity, form, jurisdiction and filing date.
Spot-check retrieval of one prior-year CGAD with its confirmation reference inside 10 minutes.
checklist.done: the filed set and its full support are archived, retention-labelled, marked confidential and retrievable within 10 minutes.

testing.step: Derive the population of required filings independently
actions: Pull the legal entity register and, for each insurance entity, read the domicile's own instructions to derive which governance disclosures were required in the year.
Build your own entity-by-form population rather than accepting the filing matrix, so an entity omitted from the matrix cannot be omitted from the test.
Reconcile your derived population to the filing calendar and list every required filing absent from the calendar as an automatic exception.
testing.done: an independently derived entity-by-form population exists and is reconciled to the filing calendar with omissions listed.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory due date
actions: For each population row read the due date rule from the current instructions — 1 June for the CGAD, 30 April or 15 days after the annual statement month for Form B depending on the state, the agreed date for the ORSA summary.
Recompute the due date yourself, including any dependency on the annual statement filing date, and compare it to the date used on the calendar.
Flag every row where the calendar date is later than your recomputed date; a wrong internal due date makes an on-time filing an accident.
Record each recomputation with the instruction page relied on.
testing.done: every due date is independently recomputed from current instructions and compared to the calendar, with later internal dates flagged.

testing.step: Trace every filing to a regulator submission confirmation
actions: For each population row retrieve the submission confirmation and read the timestamp, the receiving regulator and the tracking reference.
Confirm the document attached to the confirmation is the same version as the archived filed document by comparing page count, signature date and a spot check of the disclosure level statement.
Compute days early or late against the recomputed due date and list every late filing with its day count.
Treat a filing evidenced only by an internal email as unconfirmed and list it as an exception.
testing.done: every filing traces to a regulator confirmation matching the archived document, with days early or late computed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample for content testing
actions: Take 100% of CGADs and Form F enterprise risk reports, since they carry the governance assertions.
Take 10 further filings by seeded random selection across Form B, Form D and officer-change notifications, minimum 20 filings in total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers every CGAD and Form F plus a reproducible random draw of the remaining forms.

testing.step: Re-perform the content-to-source trace on sampled filings
actions: Take 20 factual assertions from each sampled CGAD — committee membership numbers, independence counts, meeting frequency, policy approval dates, control-function reporting lines — and trace each to the charter, register entry or minute in the board portal.
Verify every number against the composition and attendance records as at the stated reporting date, not the current position.
Treat any assertion that traces only to the prior year's filing as unsupported, and any number that disagrees with the register as a misstatement.
Capture the source document reference for each traced assertion in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled assertion is traced to a dated governance source, with unsupported or misstated items identified.

testing.step: Test the officer certification and board receipt
actions: For each sampled filing confirm the certification is signed by an officer the instructions permit, is dated on or before the submission, and uses the wording the form prescribes.
Confirm the board or designated committee minute evidencing receipt of the disclosure exists and pre-dates the certification date, since the certification asserts delivery.
Flag any certification signed after submission or supported by a minute dated later than the certification.
Confirm the confidentiality assertion was made in the form the state requires.
testing.done: every sampled certification is properly signed, dated before submission and supported by a pre-dating board receipt minute.

testing.step: Reconcile Form B and Form F content to independent records
actions: Compare the Form B organisational chart and ownership percentages to the legal entity register and to the equity ownership schedules in the statutory annual statement for the same date.
Compare the listed directors and officers to the composition register as at the reporting date.
Compare the Form F risk narrative to the board-approved ORSA and risk appetite statement and flag any material development disclosed in one and absent from the other.
List every affiliate agreement in force from the contract repository and confirm each appears on the Form B.
testing.done: Form B and Form F content is reconciled to the entity register, annual statement schedules, composition register, ORSA and contract repository.

testing.step: Sweep the year for missed event-driven triggers
actions: Build an independent event list for the year: board and officer changes from the composition register, affiliate transactions from the general ledger intercompany accounts and the contract repository, and ownership changes from Corporate Development records.
For each event determine the form required and recompute the deadline — before completion for Form A, at least 30 days before for Form D, within 30 days for officer changes.
Match each event to a filing and list every unmatched event as a missed filing exception with days overdue.
Pay particular attention to affiliate transactions recorded in the ledger but never notified, the commonest silent miss.
testing.done: an independent event list is built and matched to filings, with every missed or late event-driven filing quantified in days.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the entity, form, jurisdiction, days late or assertion misstated, and the regulatory consequence.

Assign a root cause from the taxonomy — entity omitted from matrix, wrong internal due date, source content late, assertion carried forward unsupported, certification out of sequence, event trigger not detected — and an owner.
Where a filing was missed or misstated, require an amended or catch-up filing with a General Counsel-cleared covering explanation and record the submission confirmation.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a root cause, an owner, an amended or catch-up filing where needed and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State pass or fail against the zero-tolerance items — required filing not made, filing after its statutory due date, filing without the required certification — and report the proportion of sampled assertions that traced to a dated source.
Write the conclusion on whether the group's governance disclosure obligations were met, naming any entity or jurisdiction where they were not.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, reviewed or submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the General Counsel and file the workpaper under REG-013-C23.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with zero-tolerance verdicts, an assertion-trace rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the fitness and propriety standard and the assessment conclusion for directors, officers and control-function heads; the evidence collection and record-keeping run through the Chief HR Officer's team

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 5 (Suitability of Persons) as reinforced by ICP 7 (Corporate Governance) board composition expectations, delivered locally through the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application biographical affidavit and third-party verification requirement, state holding-company notification rules for officer and director changes, the UK Senior Managers and Certification Regime fit-and-proper assessment, and Solvency II Article 42 fit-and-proper requirements with notification to the national supervisor

In-scope processes.value: Appointment and periodic re-assessment of key persons in control: board directors, the chief executive, chief financial officer, chief risk officer, chief actuary and appointed actuary, chief audit executive, head of compliance and the money-laundering reporting officer, across every insurance legal entity in the group

In-scope systems.value: Key-person register, appointment dates and annual attestations in Workday HCM; biographical affidavits and verification reports held in iManage (Legal Docs); screening run through the sanctions and adverse-media platform; regulator notifications filed through the domiciliary channel

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness and Propriety Assessment Procedure FP-07 — the in-scope position list, the four assessment limbs (competence and capability, honesty and integrity, financial soundness, time commitment and conflicts), the evidence required for each limb, the third-party verification requirement, the escalation route for an adverse finding and the annual re-attestation cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the nomination committee on the recommendation of the General Counsel; re-approved annually and on any change to a domicile's key-person definition or pre-approval requirement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Assessment completed and concluded before the appointment takes effect — never retrospectively; a third-party verification report no older than 3 years supporting each biographical affidavit; regulator notification of the appointment or resignation within 30 days in most US domiciles, with pre-approval obtained before appointment in regimes that require it; annual re-attestation for every key person by 31 March

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workday triggers an assessment task the day a candidate enters the nomination pipeline, a 30-day notification countdown the day an appointment or resignation is recorded, a 90-day alert before any verification report passes its 3-year age limit, and the annual re-attestation campaign on 1 February with a 31 March due date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments effective before the assessment concluded, verification reports older than 3 years, missing screening limbs, late or missing regulator notifications and unreturned annual attestations are logged with the person, the entity, the position and the corrective action including suspension of the appointment where required

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every adverse or qualified fitness finding, every retrospective assessment and any decision to appoint despite a disclosed matter, with the reasoning recorded for the regulator

Annual re-attestation completion must be 100% for the standing register

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-person assessment file containing the biographical affidavit, verification report, screening results, conclusion and appointing resolution, plus the key-person register showing the position held and the assessment date, producible for a licensing review, a change-of-control review or a supervisory fit-and-proper enquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel answers supervisory questions on an individual's fitness and propriety and owns any disclosure of an adverse finding; the Corporate Secretary supplies the register and appointing resolutions, and the board chair is briefed before any response concerning a sitting director

checklist.step: Define and maintain the in-scope key-person list
actions: List for each insurance legal entity the positions that are key persons in control under ICP 5 and the domicile's own definition: directors, chief executive, chief financial officer, chief risk officer, chief actuary and appointed actuary, chief audit executive, head of compliance and the money-laundering reporting officer.

Add any position the domicile designates specifically — a senior manager function under the UK regime, a Solvency II key function holder, a state-designated responsible officer — and record which regime drives it.
Tag each position in Workday so any hire, transfer or termination into or out of it raises an assessment task automatically instead of relying on someone remembering.
Review the list annually with the nomination committee and whenever a new entity or licence is added to the group.
checklist.done: every entity has a tagged key-person position list with the driving regime recorded, reviewed by the nomination committee within 12 months.

checklist.step: Open the assessment as soon as a candidate enters the pipeline
actions: Open the assessment record the day the candidate is identified — internal promotion, external hire or board nomination — and never after an offer is accepted.
Record the entity, the position, the regime driving the assessment, the intended effective date and whether the regime requires pre-approval before appointment.
Where pre-approval is required, work back from the regulator's typical determination period and tell the nomination committee the earliest lawful effective date.
Notify General Counsel and the Corporate Secretary that the assessment is open so the appointing resolution is not drafted ahead of the conclusion.
checklist.done: an assessment record exists from the day of candidate identification, carrying the regime, the pre-approval requirement and the earliest lawful effective date.

checklist.step: Collect the biographical affidavit
actions: Issue the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application biographical affidavit, or the domicile's equivalent form, to the candidate with a 10-business-day return.

Check every section is completed: full employment history with no unexplained gaps, education and professional qualifications, all present and past directorships and officerships, and each of the affirmative disclosure questions on criminal matters, regulatory action, civil litigation, bankruptcy and licence refusals.
Return any affidavit with a blank field, an unexplained gap of more than 60 days or an unsigned notarisation where the form requires it.
File the signed affidavit in the person's assessment folder with the receipt date.
checklist.done: a complete, signed and notarised affidavit is on file with no blank fields and every employment gap explained.

checklist.step: Commission the third-party verification report
actions: Engage an NAIC-accepted verification vendor to produce the third-party report supporting the affidavit — most domiciles will not accept an affidavit older than 3 years without one.

Confirm the report covers each verification element: identity, employment history, education and qualifications, criminal record, regulatory and licensing history, civil litigation, bankruptcy and media search.
Read the report against the affidavit line by line and list every discrepancy, however small — an unexplained date difference is often the thread that unravels an undisclosed matter.
Put every discrepancy to the candidate in writing and record their explanation and the supporting evidence.
checklist.done: a full third-party verification report is on file, compared line by line with the affidavit, with every discrepancy explained in writing.

checklist.step: Run the honesty and integrity screening
actions: Screen the candidate and their known close associates against the consolidated sanctions lists, politically exposed person lists and adverse media, using date of birth and known aliases rather than name alone.
Run the regulatory-action search across the domicile's own enforcement register and any prior jurisdiction the affidavit discloses.
Clear or escalate each hit with a written disposition — a discounted hit needs a recorded reason, not a silent dismissal.
Attach the screening output with its run date to the assessment folder.
checklist.done: screening across sanctions, PEP, adverse media and regulatory enforcement is complete, with every hit dispositioned in writing and dated.

checklist.step: Test financial soundness
actions: Obtain the credit and financial soundness check the regime requires, with the candidate's written consent recorded before it is run.
Review for unsatisfied judgements, bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings, tax liens and any pattern suggesting the person is not managing their own affairs soundly.
Where an adverse item appears, obtain the candidate's written explanation and any evidence of settlement, and assess whether it bears on the specific role's responsibilities.
Record the conclusion on the financial soundness limb with the reasoning, not merely a pass flag.
checklist.done: the financial soundness limb is concluded with consented checks, explanations for any adverse item and recorded reasoning.

checklist.step: Verify competence, capability and professional standing
actions: Verify claimed qualifications directly with the awarding body or the professional institute rather than accepting a certificate copy.
For actuarial and audit roles confirm current membership and good standing with the relevant professional body, and for licensed roles confirm the licence status through the appropriate registry.
Assess the candidate's experience against the specific responsibilities of the role and the collective competence gap on the board recorded in the skills matrix.
Take up at least two references covering the candidate's conduct and competence in a comparable role and record what was said.
checklist.done: qualifications and professional standing are verified at source, and the competence limb is concluded against the role's actual responsibilities with references taken.

checklist.step: Assess time commitment and conflicts
actions: List every other directorship, employment, trusteeship and significant commitment the candidate holds and estimate the total time committed against the hours this role requires.
Compare the count against any regulatory cap on concurrent directorships in the domicile and against the board's own policy.

Collect the conflicts declaration covering financial interests, related-party relationships, supplier and reinsurance connections and family relationships, and cross-check it against the group's counterparty registers.
Record where a conflict is manageable by recusal and where it disqualifies, and put the reasoning in writing.
checklist.done: time commitment is quantified against the role and any cap, and the conflicts declaration is cross-checked with a written manageable-or-disqualifying conclusion.

checklist.step: Write the assessment conclusion across all four limbs
actions: Write a single conclusion document addressing each limb — competence and capability, honesty and integrity, financial soundness, time commitment and conflicts — with the evidence relied on for each.
State the conclusion as fit and proper, fit and proper subject to stated conditions, or not fit and proper, and never leave it implied by the absence of a problem.
Where a matter was disclosed and the candidate is still recommended, set out why it does not bear on this role, since this is the paragraph a supervisor will read first.
Date and sign the conclusion before the appointment is put to the board.
checklist.done: a dated, signed conclusion addresses all four limbs with the evidence and reasoning, including any disclosed matter, before the board vote.

checklist.step: Take the appointment through the nomination committee and the board
actions: Put the assessment conclusion, the skills matrix gap it fills and the proposed effective date to the nomination committee for recommendation.
Take the recommendation to the board and record the appointing resolution with the effective date, the position and the entity.
Confirm the effective date is on or after the conclusion date and, where pre-approval is required, on or after the regulator's approval date.
Record any conditions attached to the appointment and the person responsible for monitoring them.
checklist.done: a board resolution appoints the person with an effective date at or after the assessment conclusion and any required regulatory approval.

checklist.step: Notify or seek approval from every relevant regulator
actions: For each entity the person serves, identify whether the domicile requires prior approval or post-appointment notification, and diarise the deadline — commonly within 30 days of the change for US domiciles.
Prepare and file the notification with the biographical affidavit and verification report where the domicile requires them attached, through the domiciliary channel.
For regimes requiring pre-approval, file the application and hold the appointment until the approval arrives; record the approval reference.
Capture the submission confirmation and file it with the assessment folder, and repeat the process on resignation or removal.
checklist.done: every regulator is notified or has approved inside the statutory day count, with confirmations filed for both appointment and departure.

checklist.step: Record the person on the key-person register and onboard the role
actions: Add the person to the key-person register with entity, position, regime, effective date, assessment conclusion reference, verification report date and notification reference.
Set the 3-year verification-report expiry date and the annual attestation obligation on the record.
Issue the role-specific responsibilities statement so the person has a written record of what they are accountable for, and obtain their signed acknowledgement.
Enrol them in the mandatory training curriculum for their role within the 30-day new-joiner window.
checklist.done: the register carries a complete record with expiry and attestation obligations set, a signed responsibilities acknowledgement and training enrolment.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-attestation and ongoing monitoring
actions: Launch the attestation campaign on 1 February to every person on the standing register, due 31 March, asking them to confirm nothing has changed across the four limbs and to disclose anything that has.
Re-run sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening on the whole register annually and on any name that appears in the news in between.
Refresh any third-party verification report approaching its 3-year age limit, starting 90 days before expiry.
Chase non-returns weekly from 15 March and escalate any outstanding at 31 March to the General Counsel and the committee chair.
checklist.done: the register is 100% re-attested by 31 March, re-screened annually, with verification reports refreshed before their 3-year expiry.

checklist.step: Handle an adverse finding or a change in circumstances
actions: On any disclosure, screening hit or external report affecting a sitting key person, open a review the same day and record what is known and when it became known.

Assess whether the person remains fit and proper for the specific role, taking the matter's seriousness, relevance and recency into account, and consider interim measures such as stepping back from a decision or a temporary reallocation of responsibilities.
Determine with Regulatory Counsel whether the matter is notifiable to the supervisor and file inside the required period; most regimes expect prompt notification of a material change.
Record the outcome — continue, continue with conditions, or remove — and the board's decision, and update the register and the regulator accordingly.
checklist.done: every adverse matter has a same-day review, a documented re-assessment, a notification decision and a recorded board outcome with the register updated.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment records
actions: Archive per person per role: affidavit, verification report, screening outputs, credit check consent and result, qualification verifications, references, conflicts declaration, the signed conclusion, the appointing resolution and every regulator notification, under REG-013-C24/<entity>/<person>.
Apply the 10-years-after-departure retention label and restrict access to Legal, HR leadership and Internal Audit given the personal data involved.
Confirm the archive answers 'was this person assessed before their effective date' directly from the index without opening files.
Spot-check retrieval of two prior appointments per quarter against the 5-business-day regulator standard.
checklist.done: each person's assessment file is archived with restricted access, retained 10 years after departure, and indexed to show assessment date against effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments, resignations and standing key persons
actions: Extract from Workday every hire, transfer, promotion and termination in the year into or out of a tagged key-person position, with effective dates.
Independently extract director appointments and resignations from the board minutes and the entity register, since directors are frequently not on the payroll system.
Reconcile the two sources to the key-person register and list every appointment present in one source and absent from the register as an exception.
testing.done: the appointment population is built from payroll and board records independently and reconciled to the key-person register.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of director, chief executive, chief risk officer, appointed actuary, chief audit executive and money-laundering reporting officer appointments.
Take 15 further appointments and 15 standing register records by seeded random selection, minimum 40 records in total.
Record the seed, both population sizes and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers every senior control-function appointment plus a reproducible random draw of appointments and standing records.

testing.step: Recompute the assessment-before-appointment sequence
actions: For each sampled appointment read the assessment conclusion date, the board resolution date, any regulatory approval date and the effective date from source documents rather than the register fields.
Confirm the sequence: conclusion, then resolution, then (where required) regulatory approval, then effective date — any inversion is a zero-tolerance failure.
Compute the number of days the person served before the assessment concluded, where the sequence was inverted.
Check whether any inverted case was signed off by General Counsel as a retrospective assessment and whether the regulator was told.
testing.done: the date sequence is recomputed from source documents for each sampled appointment, with any pre-assessment service quantified in days.

testing.step: Test the affidavit and verification report on each sampled file
actions: Retrieve the biographical affidavit and confirm it is signed, notarised where required, and complete with no blank affirmative-disclosure answers.
Read the employment history for gaps over 60 days and confirm each is explained on file.
Confirm a third-party verification report exists, covers all required elements, and was dated within 3 years of the appointment effective date.
Compare the report to the affidavit yourself on dates, titles and disclosed matters and list any discrepancy the assessment did not address.
testing.done: every sampled file has a complete affidavit and a current verification report, independently compared with all discrepancies accounted for.

testing.step: Re-run the integrity screening on sampled individuals
actions: Re-screen each sampled person against sanctions, PEP and adverse-media sources using date of birth and aliases, independently of the original run.
Compare your hits to the original screening output and investigate any hit the original missed or discounted.
Confirm each discounted hit on the original file carries a written reason rather than a silent clearance.
Search the domicile's enforcement register for each person and confirm nothing is outstanding that the file does not address.
testing.done: each sampled person is independently re-screened, with missed or silently discounted hits identified and enforcement registers checked.

testing.step: Test the conclusion covers all four limbs with evidence
actions: Read each sampled conclusion and confirm it addresses competence and capability, honesty and integrity, financial soundness, and time commitment and conflicts as separate reasoned findings.
Trace the evidence cited for each limb to a document in the file — a conclusion citing evidence that is not present is unsupported.
Where a matter was disclosed, confirm the conclusion explains why it does not bear on the role rather than passing over it.
Confirm the conclusion is signed and dated by a person authorised under the procedure.
testing.done: each sampled conclusion is tested limb by limb with cited evidence traced to the file and disclosed matters explicitly reasoned.

testing.step: Recompute the regulator notification day counts
actions: For each sampled appointment and resignation identify every entity and domicile requiring notification or prior approval, working from the entity register rather than the filing file.
Recompute the deadline from the effective date — commonly 30 days for US domiciliary notification — and compare it to the submission confirmation timestamp.
List every notification missing entirely, since a person can be notified in one domicile and overlooked in another where the same entity is licensed.
Confirm each pre-approval regime's approval pre-dates the effective date.
testing.done: notification deadlines are recomputed per entity and domicile, with late and missing notifications listed and pre-approvals date-checked.

testing.step: Test the standing register, re-attestation and report ageing
actions: Reconcile the standing key-person register at year end to the tagged positions in Workday and the board composition register, listing any position with no assessed holder.
Compute the annual re-attestation completion rate against the 31 March deadline and list every non-return by name and position.
Age every verification report on the register and list those over 3 years old and those with no refresh scheduled.
Confirm the annual re-screening was actually run across the whole register by checking the screening platform's run history, not the register flag.
testing.done: the standing register is reconciled, re-attestation completion computed against 31 March, and verification-report ageing and re-screening independently verified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception naming the person, entity, position and the regulatory consequence — an unassessed key person in a licensed entity can put the licence itself in question.

Assign a root cause from the taxonomy — position not tagged, assessment opened late, affidavit incomplete, verification report stale or missing, screening limb skipped, conclusion unsupported, notification missed, attestation not returned — and an owner.
Where a person served without a concluded assessment, require the assessment to be completed immediately and a General Counsel determination on regulator notification.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
